title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Fairfield University rituals spanning Stag spirit, seasonal celebrations, service, engineering, and academic milestones.

cards.title: Dress Up for Pres Ball
cards.subtitle: September dancing on Bellarmine Lawn
cards.notes: Watch the University calendar each September, then dress formally and join the student celebration outside Bellarmine Hall.
cards.short_summary: The University president hosts Fairfield students for an annual formal lawn celebration known as Pres Ball.
cards.evidence_claim: Fairfield states that its Presidential Ball began in 2004 and is held each September on the lawn of Bellarmine Hall.
cards.source_title: Fun Facts & Tips for First Year Stags!
cards.access_notes: For Fairfield students; consult the current University event calendar for the date, admission rules, and attire guidance.

cards.title: Join the Red Sea Madness Pep Rally
cards.subtitle: Fairfield's basketball-season kickoff
cards.notes: Wear Fairfield red and follow the athletics or student-life calendar for the annual team introductions, pep rally, and concert.
cards.short_summary: Basketball introductions and a fall concert merge into Fairfield's red-clad season-opening celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Fairfield documents Red Sea Madness as an annual event marking the beginning of basketball season and celebrating the men's and women's teams.
cards.source_title: Fun Facts & Tips for First Year Stags!
cards.access_notes: Check the current Fairfield athletics or student-life listing for venue, entry requirements, and event timing.

cards.entity_name: Annual Holiday Marketplace and Tree Lighting
cards.title: Count Down to the Campus Tree Lighting
cards.subtitle: Carols, Lucas, and Fairfield's holiday lights
cards.notes: Meet near the announced campus tree, listen for the student singing groups, and stay for the president-led lighting countdown.
cards.short_summary: Fairfield opens its holiday season by illuminating the campus tree during a community celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Fairfield's 2025 event page identifies the tree lighting as an annual, free, family-friendly tradition featuring the University president, student singers, and Lucas the Stag.
cards.source_title: Annual Holiday Marketplace and Tree Lighting
cards.access_notes: The cited 2025 edition was free and open to the community; verify the next edition's date and campus location before visiting.

cards.title: Close the Semester at Clam Jam
cards.subtitle: Fairfield's long-running beach celebration
cards.notes: Look for the official spring announcement and use University transportation or access instructions for the organized beach event.
cards.short_summary: Clam Jam brings Fairfield students to the beach for a supervised spring send-off before finals.
cards.evidence_claim: Fairfield describes Clam Jam as a long-standing, end-of-year tradition where students gather at Fairfield beach for food, friends, sun, and dancing.
cards.access_notes: Student event; attend only through the University's current registration, transportation, and beach-access arrangements.

cards.title: Mark the Final Week as a Stag
cards.subtitle: Service, reflection, and a Commencement Ball
cards.notes: Graduating seniors should review the official schedule early and register separately for the week's listed milestone activities.
cards.short_summary: Fairfield sends off graduating seniors with a week of friendship, reflection, service, and celebratory events.
cards.evidence_claim: Fairfield documents Senior Week as a week-long spring celebration for seniors that culminates in friendship, service, reflection, and a Commencement Ball.
cards.access_notes: Limited to eligible graduating seniors and their authorized guests where applicable; consult the current registration materials.

cards.title: Wear Red Every Fairfield Friday
cards.subtitle: A weekly Stag-spirit dress ritual
cards.notes: Pull on red or Fairfield gear each Friday; start with First Fairfield Friday's welcome events when the fall schedule is posted.
cards.short_summary: The campus turns team color into a weekly ritual, beginning with a larger first-Friday celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Fairfield's First Fairfield Friday announcement asks community members to show Stag spirit every Friday by wearing red or Fairfield gear.
cards.source_title: Mark Your Calendars for First Fairfield Friday, Sept. 6
cards.access_notes: The clothing custom is campus-wide; individual First Fairfield Friday activities may have separate eligibility or access rules.

cards.title: Engineer a Walk Across the Pool
cards.subtitle: Buoyant contraptions built by first-year teams
cards.notes: Watch for student-built devices crossing the RecPlex pool, or join through the designated Fundamentals of Engineering course team.
cards.short_summary: Engineering students turn classroom principles into a race across the pool on handmade flotation devices.
cards.evidence_claim: Fairfield's current traditions page says mostly first- and second-year student teams build contraptions using Fundamentals of Engineering skills and attempt to cross the pool.
cards.access_notes: Building and operating a device is course-based; spectators should follow current RecPlex event and pool-safety directions.

cards.title: Show Up for STAGiving Day
cards.subtitle: One Fairfield-wide day of generosity
cards.notes: Choose a documented Fairfield program to support, or share the official campaign through the listed University social channels.
cards.short_summary: Fairfield concentrates community giving and Stag stories into one annual 24-hour campaign.
cards.evidence_claim: Fairfield identifies STAGiving Day as a defining annual tradition and says its 2026 edition was a 24-hour celebration for alumni, parents, students, faculty, staff, and friends.
cards.source_title: STAGiving Day Returns March 25: A Tradition Carried Forward by Generations
cards.access_notes: Participation is community-wide and online options are available; making a financial gift is optional and requires a purchase-like contribution.

cards.title: Receive the Egan Fob Watch
cards.subtitle: Fairfield nursing's clinical rite of passage
cards.notes: Egan nursing students should attend with their cohort and look for the procession, timepiece presentation, and professional oath.
cards.short_summary: A red-scrubbed cohort receives upside-down fob watches before entering Fairfield's clinical-education phase.
cards.evidence_claim: Fairfield reports that its Clinical Initiation Ceremony marks nursing students' entry into clinical practice and culminates with students receiving fob watches and pledging an oath.
cards.source_title: Egan Nursing Students Mark Start of Clinical Education
cards.access_notes: Ceremony participation is for the designated Egan nursing cohort; family attendance depends on current invitations and venue capacity.

cards.title: Send a Bear Hug Through Fairfield
cards.subtitle: A holiday drive begun by Alumni Relations in 1999
cards.notes: Donate only a new, tagged stuffed animal during the announced collection window and follow the current mailing or drop-off directions.
cards.short_summary: Fairfield's holiday service tradition converts new stuffed animals into 'bear hugs' for children receiving care.
cards.evidence_claim: Fairfield says Teddy Bears With Love began in December 1999, is now led by the Student Alumni Association, and donates collected stuffed animals to children's hospitals and charities.
cards.access_notes: The 2026 collection is scheduled to begin November 2; participation requires acquiring a qualifying new, tagged stuffed animal.
